incidents-bot: Pager: HIGH - 10m spike in 5xxs for /v1/generate in us-east-1. Error rate ~4.2%, p95 latency up. Affected route: /v1/generate. @eng-oncall please ack and follow runbook: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/api-5xx :rotating_light:
Priya Kapoor: Ack. I'm primary for this window, taking lead. I'll start triage and post updates here.
Marco Diaz: Secondary here. If Priya needs escalation to infra/runtime/security I'll jump in.
Priya Kapoor: Quick customer-impact snapshot — initial look at logs shows retries for a subset of customers, ~40 distinct orgs with >3 errors each in last 10m. Sam, are we seeing inbound support tickets?
Sam Patel: Support seeing ~12 new tickets mentioning timeouts. Top 3 customers affected are listed in the support dashboard. I've DM'd CS leads and pinged AEs for the impacted accounts.
Priya Kapoor: Thanks. Immediate plan: 1) confirm if this is runtime/model serving or infra/network 2) apply quick mitigation (route to fallback model variant or scale) 3) notify CS. Ben, Jonah, Kara — please triage routing.
Ben Liu: Infra oncall here. I'll check LB and autoscaler. Kicking off checks: health of NLB, target group error counts, EC2/GPU host metrics, and any recent infra deploys.
Jonah Park: Runtime oncall — I'll look at model workers, queue depth, KV cache hits, and any recent model rollout changes. Also checking quantization/ops kernel changes from last deploy.
Kara Smith: Security oncall — no IDS alerts so far. I'll watch for suspicious spikes or malformed requests, but initial ask is infra/runtime.
Priya Kapoor: Running steps from runbook now: tailing logs, checking queue depth, verifying model variant fallback config. Command I'm running: ```
# tail failing worker logs
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=model-worker --since=15m | grep ERROR | tail -n 200
# check queue depth
redis-cli -h redis-prod zcard model_request_queue
```
Ben Liu: Infra note — NLB error rate matches app 5xx spike, but host CPU/mem look normal. Autoscaler did not scale because average CPU below threshold; looks like many requests are getting 503 from worker pool saturation (blocked threads). I'll validate pod metrics (goroutines/threads) and recent node-side updates.
Jonah Park: Found high model process GC/pinned threads on several pods; also a new runtime config rolled out ~20m ago that increases max_batch_size. Could be causing head-of-line blocking for smaller, low-latency requests. Rolling a quick rollback to previous config for a canary.
Priya Kapoor: Good catch. Can we roll the config rollback to remaining clusters as mitigation? If not, we can enable fallback model variant at load balancer level.
Jonah Park: I can rollback the runtime config in canary and then promote if stable. Doing canary rollback now (rolling restart of 3 pods). Will monitor error rate.
Priya Kapoor: Sam — tell CS/support we may have partial mitigation in place. We will follow up when error rate drops.
Sam Patel: Noted, messaging queued: "We're investigating increased timeouts for generation in us-east-1 and applying mitigations. ETA 15-30m."
Ben Liu: While Jonah is rolling back, I'm increasing pool size on a couple of healthy nodes to give breathing room. Command: ```
kubectl scale deploy/worker-pool --replicas=12 -n runtime
```
Alice Chen: Quick note on handoffs — Priya, you have a scheduled handoff window 03:00-05:00 UTC tomorrow where you're out. Do we need to arrange coverage or is Marco covering?
Priya Kapoor: Yes, I'll be unavailable 03:00-05:00 UTC tomorrow (calendar). Marco, can you cover that gap or should I request a swap?
Marco Diaz: I can cover the first hour (03:00-04:00 UTC) but I have a calendar conflict 04:00-05:00. If someone can cover 04:00-05:00 I'd be happy to take the earlier hour. @Alice any volunteers?
Alice Chen: I can take 04:00-05:00 UTC if needed. I'll update the oncall rota and post in #eng-oncall-handoffs.
Kara Smith: Security side — if this ends up being an exploit pattern we should kick off an incident and preserve logs. For now no indications, but please tag me if we see anomalous user agents or IP concentration.
Jonah Park: Canary rollback completed; errors in canary pods dropped to baseline within 3m. Promoting rollback to the rest of canaries now. Monitoring overall error rate — p95 and 5xx trending down.
Priya Kapoor: Great. We're seeing overall 5xx drop from 4.2% -> 0.8% in last 8 minutes. Keeping runbook open for 30m after stable.
Ben Liu: Infra will keep autoscaler thresholds under watch; also filing a follow-up to revisit max_batch_size default.
Priya Kapoor: Post-incident actions: (1) follow-up with runtime team to revert config cause permanently or tune batching, (2) update runbook with this failure mode, (3) CS postmortem notice for impacted customers. I'll file the incident ticket after we close.
Marco Diaz: Ack. I'll take primary during Priya's 03:00-04:00 gap and Alice will cover 04:00-05:00.
Priya Kapoor: Thanks team. Final note — cross-team routing: if the next page looks like worker saturation, page runtime (oncall: Jonah) first, then infra. If it's resource exhaustion at node-level, page infra first. Security only if we see anomalies. I'll add this routing rule to the runbook. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident resolved for now. Severity: elevated -> mitigated. Auto-close will occur after 30m of stability.
